A Piece of My Gaming Childhood

The first time I played Borderlands 2 was back in 2014 on my older brother’s console. And I can honestly say that it was the most amazing game I had ever played. Everything felt perfect: the gameplay, the world, the humor, and of course, the unique Borderlands style.

Now, years later, I have finally bought the complete Pandora’s Box collection on PC, and I made myself a promise: I will 100% this game!

Of course, not all the DLCs were perfect. There were a few bugs and some minor issues here and there. But honestly, that doesn’t change how much I love this game. It’s a huge piece of nostalgia for me and reminds me of a time when I could spend countless hours playing on the console and enjoying every single minute.

Even today, Borderlands 2 is incredibly fun. The characters, the story, the humor, the huge variety of weapons, and the atmosphere are simply amazing. There are very few games I can keep coming back to and still enjoy just as much as I did the first time.

To me, Borderlands 2 isn’t just a good game. It’s one of the best games I have ever played. And in my opinion, it’s by far the best Borderlands game in the entire franchise.

An absolute masterpiece that hasn’t lost any of its charm after all these years.

When you’ve managed to create an unexpectedly great first entry for a franchise, it begs the question: What the hell do you do with the sequel? In the case of Borderlands 2 developer Gearbox has decided to largely stick with what worked the first time around, while implementing a host of tweaks that make it an overall superior game. A few relatively minor complaints aside, Borderlands 2 improves not only the narrative, but almost every major game system. If you’ve been itching for a reason to jump back into the world of Pandora, Borderlands 2 provides a more than ample supply.The hook of Borderlands 2, the very reason that I found myself thinking about it when I worked or tried to fall asleep, is the loot. Guns, ammo, character skins, grenade mods, class mods -- there’s always something just a bit better, something you so desperately didn’t even know you needed until you found it in Borderlands 2. Just like Diablo or a number of other action RPGs, the hunt for loot becomes intoxicating because of the tiny rush you get each time a rare colored item spills out of a chest or is dropped by a recently slain enemy. Every firefight and intense boss battle becomes all the more rewarding, because, though you might die a few times and want to crush something near you in real life, it suddenly feels like everything is going to be OK when you’re blasting away enemies with a newly looted gun.

Also, if you are one of those clichéd nitpickers who's got problems with the "cartoonish" graphics, then my deepest condolences to you, really!

Now, if you do decide to buy the game, then only & only buy the GOTY edition. The content you get for those extra bucks is massive & completely worth it; especially you get more of Moxxi's bobs & Tina's innocence. If that's not enough then I dunno what is!

EDIT: Steam now has "Borderlands: The Handsome Collection". Buy that package instead of the GOTY because that has all the dlc's missing from the GOTY edition + The Pre Sequel.. It's a no brainer.

The #1 thing I hate about this game is how it makes "raid bosses" like the Terramorphus guy impossible to beat with one player, forcing you to socialize with other people and get them to team up with you to help beat the boss.

Overall, the art, narration and characters are really memorable. Considering I'm not much of an FPS fan (I haven't played BL1, note that), the number of hours I've put into this game is actually something I didn't plan out or expect.

First to run through was pretty fun, and somewhere halfway around the second one (if not for the DLCs), the game start to drag a little bit on solo. I particularly liked how skills can be conveniently reset anytime along side with the large variety of weapons (gun porn~!). Trying out different builds made the game really interesting to play. I also like how some quests have quirky and funny storylines.

If you're playing with friends, it's a great game to play! At this point in time, I don't think I'll be picking up BL2 again if I weren't playing with someone else. At higher levels, raid bosses get to be more frustrating than challenging, and the cycle of running through the same thing - griding and trying to score good loot just wears me out.
